title: Nonzero-register branch semantics
statement: Let a nondeterministic register program with oracle, input, and guard be fixed. Suppose its instruction at state $l$ tests whether register $r$ is zero, the guard holds at the configuration with state $l$, register values $v$, and no answer recorded, and the nonzero branch at state $l_0$ has terminating semantics with acceptance equivalent to a proposition $P$. If $v(r)\ne 0$, then the configuration at state $l$ has terminating semantics with acceptance equivalent to $P$.
hypotheses_covered: instruction at $l$ is the zero test on $r$ with branches $l_1,l_0$
nonzero successor configuration has the stated terminating semantics for $P$
